title: curie scenario manifest
description: The INPUT contract of `curie scenario <MANIFEST>`: a ticket's acceptance criteria, the bundle that answers them, and the probes that prove it. Every rule expressible here is enforced twice, in this schema and in `parse_manifest`, because a hand-written manifest never passes through a validator. The one rule this schema cannot express is cross-field: every top-level acceptance criterion must be answered by at least one POSITIVE probe, which the parser refuses by naming the uncovered criteria.

ticket.description: The ticket this scenario answers, e.g. `curie#1234`.

acceptance_criteria.description: The criterion ids the run reports against. Each must be answered by at least one positive probe.

bundle_path.description: Path to the bundle under test, resolved against the manifest's own directory.

tiers.description: The tiers to run. Only `skill` is supported today; `local` and `cluster` are known values that are refused (exit 4) rather than degraded.

model_mode.description: The model the runner must be booted on, asserted against the live container. Under `fake` nothing is graded and the run rolls up as `plumbing_ok` (ADR-0055).

probes.description: The graded turns. At least one positive probe and at least one negative control: a scenario with no control cannot be falsified.

remove_runner.description: Constrained to true: a scenario run always destroys the runner it booted. The field exists so the author acknowledges that in the checked-in artifact, not so it can be declined.

kind.description: A positive probe asserts the required behavior is present; a negative one is the control, and passes only when its grader does NOT match.

expect.description: A concrete grader mirroring the frozen `evals::Grader`, so a probe is judged by exactly the code `curie skill eval` uses.

value.description: The text to match for the text graders, or the tool NAME that must have been invoked for `tool_called`.
